prompt_text: Who does backflow testing and repair near Liberty MO?
answer_verbatim:
Several types of contractors do backflow testing and repairs near Liberty, MO — and there are easy ways to find and vet them.

Who does it
- Licensed plumbers (many general plumbing companies offer backflow testing/repair)
- Irrigation/sprinkler contractors (residential lawn systems)
- Fire-protection contractors (commercial fire sprinkler/backflow devices)
- Specialty backflow testing companies

How to find one near Liberty, MO
1. Contact the City of Liberty Water/Utilities department — they can tell you local requirements, acceptance rules for test forms, and often maintain a list of certified testers or approved contractors. (If you want, I can draft a message for you to send them.)
2. Search Google Maps/Yelp/Nextdoor for “backflow testing Liberty MO” or “backflow tester Kansas City” and filter by reviews and recent activity.
3. Check trade directories (Angi, HomeAdvisor) or local Facebook groups for recommendations.
4. Ask local irrigation or plumbing shops — many offer testing even if backflow isn’t their primary service.

What to verify before hiring
- Certification: the tester should be a certified backflow assembly tester (BAT) recognized in Missouri or by the city. Ask for certificate number and expiration date.
- License and insurance: active plumbing or contractor license and liability insurance.
- Experience with your device type and whether they work on irrigation, domestic or fire assemblies.
- They will provide a test report/form you can submit to the city (confirm whether the contractor or you must submit it).
- Written cost estimate for testing and for any required repair parts/labor.

Typical cost (ballpark)
- Testing only: roughly $60–$150 per assembly (varies by device type and region)
- Repairs: from maybe $100 for simple parts/labor to several hundred dollars if major parts or replacement assemblies are needed
- Commercial or fire-protection devices often cost more.

What to expect during a service call
- Visual inspection of the assembly
- Performing the standardized tests and recording results
- Immediate minor repairs or scheduling a repair if needed
- Completion of a test report and submission to the water authority if required

- Create a checklist for vetting contractors
- Try to find specific companies if you allow me to perform a web lookup (note: I can’t browse right now unless you paste results or allow external lookup)
